name: Dimond Library
use: Main university library; study space; Zeke's cafe
builtText: 1958 (named Dimond in 1967; known as such from 1963)
architect: 1958 architect not found; 1997–98 renovation and additions by Graham Gund Architects (Cambridge, MA)
statusNote: Student success center planned for as early as fall 2027

renovations.what: Addition (165,000 to 207,000 sf); air-conditioning, carpet, escalator and expanded stacks
$19M renovation and north and east additions by Graham Gund Architects; atrium entrance; perimeter reading rooms with vaulted ceilings and tall windows
Addison, Hubbard and Courtyard reading rooms recarpeted with refurbished furniture; new hallway flooring

facts.text: Named for Ezekiel Dimond, first full-time professor of the college, who began at the Hanover campus in 1868.
The 1998 reopening replaced a dark entrance with a soaring atrium, and cramped stacks with reading rooms with lofty vaulted ceilings and tall windows.
Reading rooms and offices sit at the perimeter for daylight with the stacks at the core: 'People like light, books don't.'
The building has had air-conditioning since the 1969 renovation.
UNH plans to co-locate tutoring, advising, accessibility and related services in a student success center in Dimond, possibly from fall 2027.

verdict: The campus's main library: a formal 1958 brick front, and inside Gund's 1998 reading rooms with timber trusses and tall windows that students rank top for study.
notes: The exhibit dates the Gund renovation to 1997 (start); it reopened Aug 31, 1998 per UNH Magazine. Search snippets show the University System seeking state money, with $15M proposed for a ~215,000 sf Dimond modernization (FY2028–29). That source spells it 'Diamond' and was not opened; the old data's '$50M phased plan' is unverified. Hours were cut in 2025 budget reductions per a TNH headline (not opened). Photos: licensed interior (Hubbard Reading Room) shows a lofty timber-trussed gable ceiling and floor-to-ceiling windows, so ceilings and light are well evidenced. The 2005 and 2018 exteriors show the Gund-era columned entrance in brick with cast-stone trim. The 2018 close-up has strong lens glare. Reddit was not reachable.
judgeNotes: Photos confirm the columned front and lantern; the Hubbard Reading Room photo justifies interior 8. Condition 6: 28 years since the Gund work, with modernization funding being sought. Dropped 05.jpg: identified only by its Flickr tags, and as a dull side-wall detail it adds little.
